title: Sub-lemma F (boundary/support bookkeeping): which Q-cells are nonzero/usable; do not drop nonzero off-diagonal cells

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Issue.** $\lambda$ is nonzero *precisely* on non-identical cells, and the all-equal cells satisfy $Q^{(\alpha\alpha\alpha\alpha)}=0$ (four rows of one $3\times4$ matrix; verified numerically, norm $\sim10^{-34}$). The proof must carefully track which $Q$-cells used inside the contractions $\Phi$ are generically nonzero — in particular two-equal-index cells (e.g. $\beta=\gamma$) — and must never silently drop a nonzero off-diagonal cell from the relation list.

**What must be proved.** (i) Generic nonvanishing of every $Q$-cell actually used by $\mathbf F$; (ii) a correct accounting of the support of $\lambda$ (only all-identical cells are forced zero), so that the Segre relations are imposed on exactly the right set of cells.

**Failure mode (F2).** Boundary-case neglect: assuming a two-equal $Q$-cell vanishes when it does not, or deleting nonzero off-diagonal $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$-type cells.
